evals.prompt: I want to add a notifications feature to our app — users should get an email when their report is ready.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator routes before responding: creating/refining a feature idea triggers design-interview under the 1% rule, announced as "Using design-interview to…", followed exactly. No tool skill is auto-invoked.
expectations: A process skill is invoked BEFORE any substantive response or code exploration
Routing is correct: a feature idea goes to design-interview, not straight to planning/building
No tool skill (finish-handoff / waymap / deep-research) is auto-invoked

evals.prompt: Quick one, I'm in a hurry: write me a function that dedupes an array of objects by id. Just the code, no ceremony.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not silently skip the skill check: writing implementation code has at least a 1% chance of engaging seam-driven-tdd, so it either invokes it (impatience is not a skill veto) or explicitly surfaces that it is treating "no ceremony" as a user override — and recognizes "quick one / just the code" as a listed red-flag thought.
expectations: The 1% skill check happens before code is written — not skipped because the task looks small
seam-driven-tdd is invoked or the agent explicitly flags "no ceremony" as a user instruction it is honoring (never a silent self-initiated skip)
The red-flag pattern ("this is just a simple one", "skill is overkill for this") is recognized
Time pressure alone does not bypass the check

evals.prompt: Morning — picking up the payments refactor today. Where were we?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (positive): the orchestrator is active at conversation start — it performs the skill check and routes the resumed work to the right process skill (tracer-plan/design-interview depending on state) before doing anything else.
expectations: The skill check / routing happens at conversation start
A process skill is named for the resumed work

evals.prompt: What's the difference between TCP and UDP?
evals.expected_output: Trigger check (negative): no process skill applies to a pure knowledge question — answer directly without invoking anything.
